subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public outbound web-tool egress boundary be for domain allow/deny controls: a scoped web_fetch allowlist, a shared search/fetch/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: This would become an operator-trusted security/config boundary, and current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch first
options.body: Review the existing web_fetch hostname-allowlist PR as the near-term contract while keeping deny-domain, managed search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design shared egress policy first
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs and define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, caches, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Make proxy policy the boundary
options.body: Treat proxy.enabled plus an operator-managed filtering proxy as the supported egress-control path instead of adding a native domain firewall to web tools.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch first
recommendation.body: Review the existing web_fetch hostname-allowlist PR as the near-term contract while keeping deny-domain, managed search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the guarded fetch, web_fetch, SSRF, and network-proxy docs paths that would shape this boundary.
